what: Instead of the cursor, two white eyes (28px diameter, 16px pupils) float fixed and follow each frame by 40% of the remaining distance to the cursor. Over a link or button the front eye grows to 1.5x and shifts 5px left, and the pupil becomes a chevron arrow (.3s ease-in-out). They appear in .2s when the mouse first moves, and hide over areas set with hide (Footer) or outside the window. Not attached on touch devices

options.targets: Selector for elements whose front eye turns into an arrow, default a, button, [data-stalker]
options.hide: Element to hide on top of it (selector), default none — brand uses the footer
options.--fx-white · --fx-ink: Sclera and pupil colors (via style), default --kf-surface · --kf-ink
options.[data-fx-part=eyes]: Row holding two eyes — child [data-fx-part=eye] Two
options.[data-fx-part=mark]: (If present) small graphic placed over the eyes (insect antennae, etc.)
options.skip: Selector for places inside targets where the previous eye should not change, none by default — in one demo: slick arrows and in-page shortcuts

from.where: shared.js .bt-stalker (original .mouse-stalker — lerp .4 · mouse-stalker--hover over links · stalker-none over the footer)

note: The original lays an insect photo over the eye — the artwork from the author’s side goes into the mark slot
